第 56 章 Navigating the Bumpy Road from Engineer to Manager走好从工程师到经理的颠簸路

Jean Hsu / 让·徐

— 第 163 页 —

The transition from engineer to engineering manager is rough. Coding is a fairly objective process, or at least it's treated like one. Many companies track the crude metrics of number of lines of code added or number of commits. The path to seniority is fairly clear in terms of the work—building, debugging, maintaining, and being a core contributor for larger and larger projects. There are some nuances, but generally speaking, at the end of the day, if you've had a big chunk of heads-down coding time, and merged a handful of pull requests, it was a good day. Most of the uncertainty around the technical path comes not from the work itself but from titles, compensation, and perceived career progression.

从工程师到工程经理的转变是艰难的。编码是一个相当客观的过程，或者至少被当作一个客观过程。很多公司追踪添加代码行数或提交次数这种粗糙指标。在工作内容上，通往资深的道路相当清楚——构建、调试、维护，在越来越大的项目中做核心贡献者。有一些细微差别，但一般来说，一天结束时，如果你有一大段埋头编码时间、合并了几个 PR，那就是好日子。技术路径的大部分不确定性不来自工作本身，而来自头衔、薪酬和感知的职业发展。

Managing people and teams is a much more subjective process, so much so that companies routinely try to have "no managers—a completely flat organization!" A lot of management is the less-visible things, and the default feedback loop for these are much longer. Progression along this path is much more unknown. No wonder the transition is so difficult. Most first-time managers don't get any support. Many senior engineers decide to move back to the hands-on technical work after a few years of managing people and teams—you might hear, "never again" or "management wasn't for me, I just want to code." A large swath of questions and blog posts around moving to engineering management are more or less variations of: How do I keep my technical edge?

管理人员和团队是一个主观得多的过程，以至于公司经常尝试「没有经理——完全扁平的组织！」很多管理是不太可见的事情，而这些的默认反馈回路长得多。沿这条路的发展要未知得多。难怪转变这么难。大多数第一次当经理的人得不到任何支持。很多高级工程师在管理人员和团队几年后决定回到动手的技术工作——你可能听到「再也不了」或「管理不适合我，我只想写代码」。关于转工程管理的大量问题和博客文章或多或少都是这个的变体：我怎么保持技术优势？

— 第 164 页 —

This question is symptomatic of a more fundamental problem, which is that these first-time engineering managers are not getting guidance in seeing the impact and rewards of moving into a management role. Dealing with the anxiety and sense of being unproductive, of course they grasp at and gravitate to the much more objectively rewarding work of coding. So, how can we pave the road so that it's not as bumpy? Making that transition smoothly requires a fundamental mindset shift in how you view your own productivity and self-worth. If you are someone in this transition, keep reading to explore some ways to make it smoother.

这个问题是一个更根本问题的症状，即这些第一次当工程经理的人没有得到指导去看到转入管理角色的影响和回报。应对着焦虑和不高效的感觉，他们当然会抓住和被编码这种客观回报多得多的工作吸引。那我们怎么铺路让它不那么颠簸？顺利完成这个转变需要在你如何看待自己生产力和自我价值上做根本的心态转变。如果你正处于这个转变中，继续读下去探索一些让它更顺利的方法。

Self: Keep a Log自我：记日志

At the end of each day, jot down the most impactful thing you did that day. Let yourself generously speculate about possible downstream effects. It can help highlight the potential impact of your actions when things seem very chaotic and uncertain. Example: Today I had a meaningful one-on-one with Alice and helped her see how important her work is to the team's purpose and overall goals. The increased alignment could make her more motivated and productive, which might increase team morale, as well. Example: Bob came to me with an interpersonal issue that he was struggling with. I coached him to give feedback in a kind way. He pinged me on Slack in the afternoon that the conversation had gone really well. Now he has that skill in his toolbelt for future challenging situations. And he has one successful example in which he took initiative to change something that's not working.

每天结束时，草草记下你那天做的最有影响的事。让自己慷慨地推测可能的下游影响。当事情看起来非常混乱和不确定时，它可以帮突出你行动的潜在影响。例子：今天我和 Alice 进行了有意义的一对一，帮她看到她的工作对团队目的和整体目标有多重要。增强的对齐可能让她更有动力和生产力，也可能提升团队士气。例子：Bob 带着一个他在挣扎的人际问题来找我。我辅导他用友善的方式给反馈。下午他在 Slack 上 ping 我说对话进行得很好。现在他工具箱里有了这个技能应对未来的挑战情境。而且他有了一个成功例子——他主动改变了不工作的事情。

Internal: Find Peer Support内部：找同伴支持

One or a group of trusted peers can act as a sounding board. Being able to post something like, "Hey, I have this situation, and here's how I'm thinking of approaching it. Am I missing anything?" in a confidential setting is extremely valuable. Senior managers can coach first-time managers, and first-time managers can commiserate together and then help one another through the rough times. Peer support in a company—someone you can reach out to and say, "Do you have 10 min? I want to run something by you"—is ideal. At smaller companies, this is often not possible, so having an explicit external peer relationship can also be very useful, especially for sharing best practices and perspectives across companies.

一个或一群信任的同伴可以作为共鸣板。在保密环境中能发「嘿，我有这个情况，这是我想的处理方式。我漏了什么吗？」这种东西极其有价值。高级经理可以辅导第一次当经理的人，第一次当经理的人可以一起诉苦然后互相帮助度过艰难时期。公司内的同伴支持——一个你可以联系说「你有 10 分钟吗？我想跟你说个事」的人——是理想的。在小公司这通常不可能，所以有明确的外部同伴关系也可能非常有用，尤其是跨公司分享最佳实践和视角。

— 第 165 页 —

External: Work with a Coach外部：和教练合作

As an engineering leadership coach, my job is not to convince people that management is or isn't the way forward. A good coach can shine a light on someone's strengths, areas for improvement, and the rewards and impact of that management path so that they can make an informed decision. Many potentially great managers go back to primarily IC work because of inadequate support, and they don't have anyone to bring the management path into as clear a focus as the technical path. The path can be dark and bumpy at times, but having grounding anchors of support can set you up for the journey ahead while you get your footing.

作为工程领导教练，我的工作不是说服人们管理是不是前进的路。好的教练可以照亮一个人的优势、改进领域、以及那条管理道路的回报和影响，让他们做出知情决定。很多潜在的优秀经理因为支持不足回到主要做 IC 工作，他们没有人把管理道路带到和技术道路一样清晰的焦点。这条路有时可能黑暗和颠簸，但有支持的锚点可以在你站稳脚跟时为前方旅程做好准备。
